one_liner: Otter.ai has a REST public API (bearer API keys) for Enterprise workspaces only, via the account manager. It also has a vendor-hosted, OAuth-protected MCP server at mcp.otter.ai/mcp.
auth_notes: The REST API uses bearer API keys created under Integrations → Developer (max 2 per user). The MCP server uses OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration, so no developer app or client secret is needed. That OAuth path covers MCP only, not the REST API. The connect.tryotter.com pages describe the Otter restaurant platform, a different product, and were ignored.
access_notes: The REST public API is for Enterprise workspaces. If it is not visible, the docs say to contact the Otter account manager. No free path to API credentials is documented. Whether the MCP server is open to non-Enterprise plans is not stated in the pages.
blocker_notes: REST API access requires an Enterprise plan and enablement through the account manager. The MCP server is hosted on the vendor's own domain and supports self-serve OAuth, but its tool set and plan availability are not documented in the fetched pages. It could offer a lighter path, which is unverified. The MCP Registry shows nothing under the vendor namespace.

evidence.quote: All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication.
Note**: There is a limit of 2 API keys per user.
The server supports OAuth Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), so the client registers itself automatically
